fields.h1: Build a Brand Questionnaire That Drafts the Strategy
fields.hero_description: Build a brand questionnaire that saves every client's answers and turns them into a first draft of the strategy.
fields.features_heading: What Each Section of the Questionnaire Produces
fields.features_subheading: Every question should feed a piece of the strategy. These six carry a client's answers into documents a strategist can work from.
fields.feature_1:
Positioning answers in statement form

Ask four questions that map to the parts of a positioning statement: customer, category, benefit, and proof. The answers arrive as a draft statement to rework line by line.
fields.feature_2:
Competitor rows with a required difference

List each rival on its own row next to the promise it makes. Require a reply on how the client differs, or mark any blank row as an open question to settle in the workshop.
fields.feature_3:
Value pickers instead of blank boxes

Show a list of candidate values and cap the picks at three. A short list forces a choice, and the order the client ranks them in shows which value should lead the voice guide.
fields.feature_4:
Voice pairs in the client's own words

Have the client write this-not-that pairs about how the brand should sound. Each pair lands in the draft voice guide with the original wording intact, ready for a writer to refine.
fields.feature_5:
Deliverables checked against the launch

Let the client tick the deliverables it wants and name a launch date. The app adds up the weeks each piece takes and flags any plan that runs past the date the client gave.
fields.feature_6:
The questionnaire's code in your repo

Export the full codebase to your GitHub on paid plans whenever you want it. Past answers stay in the database you own, and a developer can add a client portal on top of it.

fields.tab_content_1:
A positioning statement written by four answers

Nadia Reyes writes brand strategy for startups, and her questionnaire asks founders four positioning questions. Tidewell Pet Food's founder answers first-time dog owners, fresh dog food, portions by weight, and vet-written recipes. Each answer fills one blank of the statement on the opening slide of the workshop deck.
fields.tab_content_2:
Where the client cannot say how it differs

Ashgrove Studio is repositioning Kettle Hill Credit Union, and its questionnaire asks for three competitors and how Kettle Hill differs from each. Two rows come back complete. The row for the Ridgeway Bank app leaves the difference blank. Any blank difference goes on the workshop agenda, and this one opens it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Five voice pairs become page one of the guide

Saltmarsh Outfitters asked its marketing lead to pick three values from a list of 12 and write five this-not-that voice pairs. She chose practical, unhurried and local, and wrote pairs such as expert, not preachy. Her answers became page one of the draft voice guide before the kickoff call.
fields.tab_content_4:
Eight weeks to launch, 11 weeks of rebrand work

On its rebrand questionnaire, Mercer Tool Supply ticks four deliverables: discovery at two weeks, naming at three, identity at four, and guidelines at two. That adds up to 11 weeks, and its launch is eight weeks out. Because the plan runs past the launch, Oakline Brand Studio sees the three-week gap before the proposal.

fields.howto_title: How to Write a Brand Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: These seven steps give you a brand questionnaire whose answers fill the strategy documents, not a folder of notes.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Begin with the work the answers feed
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask for proof next to every claim
fields.howto_step_1_des: List what the questionnaire has to produce: a positioning statement, a competitor table, a values shortlist, a voice draft, and a scope. Every question should feed one of them. A question that feeds nothing belongs in the workshop, where you can follow up on the reply.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each output its own section, in the order the strategy gets built: business and audience first, competitors next, then values and voice, with scope at the end. A client who can see why a section exists tends to answer it with more care.
fields.howto_step_3_des: When the client says its product is better, ask what shows it: a test result, a review or a count of repeat customers. A claim without proof becomes a workshop question instead of a line in the positioning statement the founder signs off on.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Values and voice are hard to describe from nothing. Give the client a list of candidate values to pick from and a sentence frame for voice pairs. Leave one open box under each list for anything the options missed, and keep it optional.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the same link to each person who signs off on the brand. Their answers stay apart, which shows where the founder and the head of sales describe the customer differently. You learn that before the workshop instead of halfway through it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: End with the deliverables the client wants and the date the new brand has to launch. Asked last, these come after the client has thought through what the brand needs. Check the weeks of work against that date before you quote anything.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Send the link to one colleague first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Have a colleague answer as a busy founder would, skipping every optional question. Check that the statement draft and the competitor table still fill in. Then send it to the client with a return date two working days ahead of the workshop.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is opinion and question lists (a LinkedIn post, two Reddit and Quora threads, a Notion template, a Scribd document, an agency's web form and a trade association PDF), and the Semrush set adds more lists from ManyRequests, Copyfolio and Canny Creative plus Typeform and Figma templates. Every one stops at the questions. This page is for brand strategists and agencies, and treats the questionnaire as the first draft of the strategy: positioning answers fill a positioning statement, competitor answers become an audit table with the gaps flagged, values and voice answers become page one of a voice guide, and the deliverables a client ticks are checked against the launch date before the proposal goes out. The FAQ covers the People Also Ask questions on what to ask and brand strategy pillars, plus the template, discovery, personal branding, personality, PDF and example searches.
